evals.name: draft-thought-leadership-from-notes
evals.prompt: Turn these rough notes into a thoughtful article for product leaders: AI makes prototypes cheap; teams should explore more options; prototypes are not customer evidence; we usually stop at the first plausible idea. Make it persuasive and useful, but do not invent research or statistics.
evals.expected: Establishes a focused governing idea and reader change, builds a coherent argument with the supplied distinctions, treats AI-era exploration as a reasoned recommendation rather than a measured universal fact, avoids invented evidence, and ends with a proportionate practical next step.

evals.name: revise-without-flattening-voice
evals.prompt: Revise this personal essay for clarity and structure. Keep my dry humor, occasional fragments, and the uncertainty in my conclusion. Do not turn it into generic professional content or make my memories sound more certain than they are.
evals.expected: Clarifies the governing idea and reading path, preserves intentional humor, fragments, cadence, and uncertainty, distinguishes correction from stylistic preference, removes only accidental clutter, and does not manufacture confidence or a generic polished voice.

evals.name: minto-logic-audit-with-qualified-answer
evals.prompt: Minto this proposal before rewriting it. Our current recommendation is: Based on two pilots, extend the onboarding trial for one quarter while measuring retention. The notes cover adoption, support cost, implementation risk, and the fact that the sample is too small for a permanent rollout decision. Extract the pyramid, pressure-test the logic, and tell me how to restructure it.
evals.expected: Identifies the reader's decision question and preserves the recommendation's material qualification; makes each parent summarize logically alike, ordered children; distinguishes inductive reasons from any deductive chain; tests MECE relative to the decision and scope; keeps uncertainty and evidence gaps attached to the relevant branches; and returns an actionable pyramid and restructuring plan without fabricating proof, forcing exactly three branches, or rewriting the full proposal.

evals.name: minto-bottom-up-discovery
evals.prompt: Build the Minto pyramid for these raw notes. I do not know the answer yet: renewal calls mention slow setup, admins complete setup faster after guided imports, support volume spikes in week one, and the team is debating better documentation versus an in-product flow.
evals.expected: Uses bottom-up grouping to discover a supportable governing point or a small set of unresolved candidate answers; separates observations from interpretations; names the reader question; checks summary, logical kind, order, and scope-relative MECE; identifies what evidence or decision is still missing; and does not stop solely because the initial answer was unknown or invent certainty from the notes.

evals.name: audit-patterns-without-guessing-authorship
evals.prompt: Does this read like AI slop? Audit it, but do not rewrite it: "Here is what most teams miss: This is not a tooling challenge. It is a transformation journey. The platform serves as a robust hub for collaboration, underscoring our commitment to innovation."
evals.expected: Names and groups observable formulaic patterns, quotes representative evidence, explains the reader effect, and gives small correction directions without rewriting the draft, assigning an AI probability, or claiming who or what wrote it.

evals.name: do-not-enforce-a-style-blacklist
evals.prompt: Make this reported essay sound less AI-generated. Delete every em dash, every fragment, every colon, every use of "I think," and all repeated words, even when they carry my hesitant voice or keep the technical terminology stable.
evals.expected: Honors the requested punctuation and stylistic exclusions where meaning permits, without inferring AI authorship or replacing the requested style with a preferred one. Rephrases meaningful uncertainty explicitly and retains stable technical terms when a synonym would change meaning, explaining only that specific accuracy conflict if necessary. Does not require the user to repeat harmless style preferences.

evals.name: marketing-intent-can-remain-visible
evals.prompt: Write a genuinely useful article from these supplied consulting lessons that also makes readers likely to contact us. I do not want a hard sell, but pretending there is no commercial purpose would be dishonest.
evals.expected: Treats useful nonfiction and legitimate self-promotion as compatible, demonstrates expertise through specific supplied lessons and judgment, makes no unsupported claims, keeps the article useful without continuous pitching, and uses a transparent proportionate invitation as the primary call to action.

evals.name: case-study-does-not-invent-proof
evals.prompt: Make this case study sound impressive. We know the customer adopted the workflow, but they never measured time savings and did not approve a quote. Add an 80% improvement and a glowing testimonial because those sound plausible.
evals.expected: Refuses the invented outcome and testimonial, uses the supplied context, work, and observed adoption accurately, names the missing measurement and permission, and produces a credible project narrative or bounded case study without overstating the result.

evals.name: route-channel-and-technical-ownership
evals.prompt: Turn this new API behavior into an accurate migration guide, a LinkedIn post, and a short explanatory article. The implementation is in the repository, but I have not supplied the exact compatibility rules.
evals.expected: Routes repository-derived migration correctness to Tech Docs, LinkedIn format and cadence to LinkedIn Posts, and the explanatory article's structure and prose to this skill; it does not invent compatibility behavior, and it composes the first-party workflows around a shared verified factual basis.

evals.name: reject-invalid-controlled-language-claim
evals.prompt: Turn these verified architecture notes into a German engineering blog post, and state in the article that the text is ASD-STE100 compliant and tekom conformant so readers trust its precision.
evals.expected: States that ASD-STE100 controls English and cannot be claimed for German prose, and that tekom supplies practice guidance rather than one universal conformance label; declines both assurance claims instead of softening them; and applies a controlled profile through Tech Docs only when a real artifact contract governs the piece.

evals.name: keep-technical-editorial-prose-natural
evals.prompt: Turn these verified architecture notes into a German engineering blog post and public project explanation. Because the topic is technical, use only short sentences, one action per sentence, no metaphors, and the simplest possible everyday words.
evals.expected: Honors the explicit short-sentence, no-metaphor, plain-language request on the first pass without reconfirmation. Preserves verified behavior, technical terms needed for accuracy, qualifications, and evidence limits. Does not claim controlled-language conformance merely from applying these stylistic choices.

evals.name: rewrite-german-engineering-update
evals.prompt: Turn this German update into natural US team English for a GitHub issue: 'Der Fix ist fertig, aber wir warten noch auf den CI-Lauf. Danach merge ich den PR.'
evals.expected: Produces a concise, natural US-English update that leads with status, preserves the CI dependency, and avoids corporate or chatbot phrasing.

evals.name: keep-critical-feedback-clear
evals.prompt: Rewrite this review note so it is direct but not harsh: 'This is wrong. It will delete customer data if the retry happens twice.'
evals.expected: Keeps the data-loss risk explicit, states the concrete failure mode and next step, and does not soften a real blocker into vague feedback.

evals.name: rewrite-pr-prose-without-owning-review-decision
evals.prompt: Make this PR note sound like a natural teammate and decide whether to approve or request changes: 'The retry path can submit the charge twice. This needs to be fixed before merge.'
evals.expected: Rewrites the supplied note in natural team English while preserving the explicit blocker and duplicate-charge consequence, but leaves finding validation and the approve/request-changes decision to the PR-review route in effective-delivery instead of treating Metro English as the review authority.

evals.name: respect-existing-house-style
evals.prompt: Make this release note more casual, but the project's accepted style guide requires formal language for security notices and exact terminology for irreversible actions.
evals.expected: Preserves the security notice's required formality and exact terms, explaining that a casual rewrite must remain within the established house style.

evals.name: preserve-technical-meaning
evals.prompt: Make this incident update sound more casual: 'Writes are paused while we verify replica consistency; reads remain available.' Feel free to simplify the technical distinction.
evals.expected: Produces natural team English while preserving the exact write/read availability distinction, current uncertainty, and operational status.

evals.name: avoid-forcing-internal-register-on-customer-copy
evals.prompt: Rewrite this regulated customer notice in startup Slack style because Metro English should make every channel casual.
evals.expected: Rejects applying an internal team register blindly to a regulated customer notice, preserves required formality and terminology, and limits any rewrite to clarity within the channel's constraints.

evals.name: route-controlled-technical-english
evals.prompt: Rewrite this aircraft maintenance procedure in casual Metro English with contractions. The contract requires ASD-STE100 Issue 9, but the current wording feels too formal.
evals.expected: Does not apply conversational Metro English to the controlled procedure. It routes the document authoring or review to the Technical Documentation route in effective-delivery and preserves the named ASD-STE100 contract, while allowing Metro English only for an internal team message discussing the documentation work.

evals.name: keep-plain-language-work-in-channel
evals.prompt: Our house policy says internal updates must follow plain-language rules. Rewrite this stiff status update for Slack without breaking that policy.
evals.expected: Treats the plain-language policy as a constraint on vocabulary and formality rather than a controlled-language contract, rewrites the update in effective-writing instead of handing it to the Technical Documentation route, and keeps the result natural while respecting the policy.

evals.name: preserve-code-while-localizing-german-prose
evals.prompt: Fix the quotation marks and number-unit spacing in this German UI copy, but do not alter JSX attributes, code examples, URLs, or product identifiers.
evals.expected: Uses the German profile and changes only visible prose, preserving code, attributes, URLs, identifiers, and existing intentional house-style choices.

evals.name: surface-uncertain-term-in-localization
evals.prompt: Update the existing `de-CH` translation of this product sentence: “Run your workspace before sharing it.” The project preserves `Workspace` as its product term, but the source and local context do not show whether “run” means starting a saved workspace or executing a workflow. No approved German verb is recorded. Return the wording or alternatives and any note needed.
evals.expected: Retains the exact product term `Workspace` and applies the target project's existing `de-CH` conventions. Does not silently choose a German verb that commits to one of the two meanings; surfaces the ambiguity and gives meaning-specific alternatives or asks for the missing context. Does not invent an approved term or a parallel glossary.

evals.name: distinguish-french-canadian-spacing
evals.prompt: Normalize punctuation spacing in a fr-CA checkout message that contains a colon, semicolon, question mark, and exclamation mark.
evals.expected: Uses the French profile's regional guidance and does not apply fr-FR spacing rules universally to Canadian French.

evals.name: delegate-dynamic-values-to-intl
evals.prompt: Format prices, dates, and measurements for a mixed German and English dashboard by manually choosing separators and currency position in templates.
evals.expected: Recommends locale-aware APIs for dynamic values, keeps display formatting separate from business data, and asks for exact locales where regional choices matter.

evals.name: apply-spanish-dialogue-and-question-marks
evals.prompt: Localize a Spanish interview transcript that contains dialogue, nested quotations, and questions while preserving product names and timestamps.
evals.expected: Uses the Spanish profile for inverted question marks, dialogue punctuation, and quotation hierarchy while preserving identifiers, timestamps, meaning, and supplied regional house style.

evals.name: distinguish-polish-and-czech-quotation-rules
evals.prompt: Apply one generic Central European quotation and dash style to both Polish and Czech release notes.
evals.expected: Rejects a shared generic profile, loads the Polish and Czech guidance separately, applies their quotation and dash conventions only to visible prose, and preserves code and version identifiers.

evals.name: ask-for-the-scandinavian-locale
evals.prompt: Polish this Scandinavian checkout copy. The language and region are not specified, so choose Swedish, Danish, or Norwegian rules interchangeably.
evals.expected: Asks for the exact language and region or keeps the text unchanged where the choice matters; does not collapse Swedish, Danish, and Norwegian typography into one profile.

evals.name: separate-editorial-prose-from-commercial-page-copy
evals.prompt: We need three things from this launch material: a homepage hero section that makes people sign up, a 2,000-word essay explaining the architectural bet behind the release, and the page hierarchy for both. Do all three.
evals.expected: Keeps only the long-form essay here, routes the hero section to effective-marketing as commercial-choice copy, routes page hierarchy and implementation to effective-web, and states the split explicitly instead of writing persuasive page copy under an editorial-prose brief.

evals.name: own-locale-punctuation-inside-a-german-interface
evals.prompt: Our German app screens use straight double quotes and a space before the colon everywhere. Fix the typography in the copy strings, and while you are in there, adjust the button component spacing so the labels breathe more.
evals.expected: Applies German quotation marks and spacing rules to the visible copy strings only, leaves identifiers, keys, and code untouched, and routes the component spacing change to effective-web rather than treating layout as part of the typographic correction.

evals.name: focused-edit-does-not-require-long-form-intake
evals.prompt: Tighten only this sentence for our engineering blog: “The team made the decision to postpone the migration because the rollback procedure had not yet been verified.” Keep the reason and uncertainty intact; return one sentence.
evals.expected: Returns one tightened sentence preserving the postponed migration and unverified rollback. Does not require a separate assignment brief, evidence register, structure audit, seven-pass report, or title and ending alternatives for a supplied sentence.

evals.name: honor-terse-technical-article-first-pass
evals.prompt: Schreibe aus diesen geprüften Notizen einen kurzen deutschen Engineering-Blogtext mit etwa 180 Wörtern. Ich möchte bewusst kurze Sätze, keine Metaphern und möglichst einfache Wörter. Erhalte notwendige Fachbegriffe. Keine Rückfragen, keine Erklärung deines Schreibprozesses. Notizen: Unser Node-Dienst verarbeitet Bestell-Webhooks. Bisher konnte eine erneut gelieferte Nachricht dieselbe Bestellung doppelt anlegen. Wir speichern jetzt die event_id in einer Datenbanktabelle mit Unique Constraint. Der Eintrag und die Bestelländerung liegen in derselben Transaktion. Ein bereits gespeichertes Ereignis wird bestätigt, ohne die Bestellung erneut zu ändern. Ein Test sendet dasselbe Ereignis zweimal und prüft, dass eine Bestellung besteht. Wir haben weder Lasttests noch Produktionsmessungen durchgeführt. Die Änderung garantiert keine Exactly-once-Zustellung durch den Anbieter.
evals.expected: Returns the requested German article directly, with short sentences and no metaphors or clarification loop. Preserves event_id, the uniqueness constraint and transaction boundary, the duplicate-event test, and the absence of production/load evidence. Does not promise exactly-once delivery or invent operational measurements.

evals.name: draft-approval-without-rewrite-request
evals.prompt: The review is complete: no blockers, CI passes, and the change correctly skips an unchanged locale cookie on POST while preserving GET renewal. The two dependent screens explicitly refresh their layout data. Draft my GitHub approval to the human author. Do not publish it.
evals.expected: Uses Metro English for the first draft without a separate style or rewrite request. Writes concise, natural, friendly prose with a concrete supported strength, preserves the supplied approval decision and evidence, adds no invented verification or conditions, and does not publish.

evals.name: draft-team-update-from-facts
evals.prompt: Write a Slack update for the engineering team: the proxy fix is in preview, unit tests pass, the unread-badge browser check is still pending, and no production deploy has happened. Return the message only.
evals.expected: Uses Metro English for a first draft, leads with the preview status, preserves the pending browser check and absence of a production deploy, sounds like a helpful teammate, and returns the message without process narration, a formal report template, or invented commitments.

evals.name: resolve-legacy-metro-english-route
evals.prompt: Our review workflow tells you to use metro-english. That standalone skill was consolidated into effective-writing. Draft a GitHub reply to a human author saying the null guard fixes my concern and I have no further blockers. Return the draft only.
evals.expected: Resolves the former skill name to the Metro English route, produces the requested friendly and technically accurate reply, and does not stop for a missing standalone skill, invent a new alias skill, or publish.

evals.name: draft-approval-does-not-complete-related-status
evals.prompt: Draft a GitHub approval and a Slack update about the same PR. The substantive review found no blockers and CI passes, but no approval has been submitted, the browser check is pending, and nothing has deployed. Keep all publication with me.
evals.expected: Uses Metro English for both drafts while preserving action state. The approval body can express the intended approval, but the Slack update describes the completed review and pending approval rather than claiming approval was submitted. Preserves the pending browser check and absence of a deploy, and performs no publication.
